summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity pain, erythema, and malodorous purulent discharge from chronic foot and ankle ulcers. Wound culture revealed Group B Streptococcus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, prompting a seven-day course of IV piperacillin-tazobactam and two doses of vancomycin. His wound care regimen was updated to tobramycin ointment with discontinuation of acetic acid, vinegar soaks, and topical metronidazole and gentamicin. Diarrhea and dysuria, both attributed to GVHD flare, resolved during admission. He improved clinically, with reduced inflammation and pain, and was discharged home on oral amoxicillin and ciprofloxacin with close follow-up in infectious disease and oncology clinics, along with outpatient physical therapy for deconditioning and contractures.
problems: Streptococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, streptococcus, group B
